standard: C# and .NET 8 Security Best Practices Guide

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / STIG V-222645: MD5 is cryptographically broken and not FIPS-compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA256.Create() or SHA384.Create() for FIPS 140-3 compliance.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-131A: SHA-1 is deprecated and not FIPS 140-3 compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA256.Create() or stronger.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / STIG V-222645: DES is cryptographically broken and forbidden by FIPS 140-3.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with AesGcm for authenticated encryption (AES-256-GCM).

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3: 3DES (TDEA) is deprecated by NIST SP 800-131A and should not be used.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with AesGcm (AES-256-GCM) for FIPS 140-3 compliant authenticated encryption.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3: RC2 is a broken cipher forbidden by FIPS 140-3.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with AesGcm (AES-256-GCM).

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03: SQL query constructed via string concatenation is vulnerable to SQL injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use parameterized queries via SqlCommand with SqlParameter: cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@id", userId), or use EF Core with LINQ.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03: Process.Start() with string concatenation can enable command injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use ProcessStartInfo with separate FileName and Arguments properties, and validate all inputs before passing to Process.Start.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A02 / NIST SC-8: Bypassing TLS certificate validation enables man-in-the-middle attacks.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove the certificate bypass callback. Use proper certificate pinning or ensure valid CA-signed certificates are deployed.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded password detected in source code.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords. Use IConfiguration and environment variables or Azure Key Vault / AWS Secrets Manager.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded password in appsettings/config detected.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove credentials from appsettings.json. Use Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, or environment variable injection.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A08 / Microsoft Security Advisory: BinaryFormatter is unsafe and must not be used for deserialization.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json, XmlSerializer, or another safe serializer. BinaryFormatter is disabled by default in .NET 7+.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-90A: System.Random is not cryptographically secure.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes() or RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32() (System.Security.Cryptography) for security-sensitive random values.

forbidden_patterns.reason: STIG: Suppressing security-related code analysis warnings (SQL injection, weak crypto, TLS) is not permitted.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Fix the underlying security issue instead of suppressing the warning. Approved suppressions require documented security review.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG V-222602: Rendering unsanitized HTML output bypasses the Razor engine's automatic encoding and enables Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Avoid Html.Raw(). Use the Razor @variable syntax for automatic HTML-encoding, or use HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode() before rendering user-controlled content.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A01 / NIST SI-10: The [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] attribute disables CSRF validation on an action, allowing cross-site request forgery attacks.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]. Ensure all state-changing endpoints are protected by [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] or the global antiforgery filter.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A02 / DISA STIG V-222575: Setting HttpOnly = false allows JavaScript to access the cookie, enabling cookie theft via XSS.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Set HttpOnly = true on all authentication and session cookies to block JavaScript access.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A02 / DISA STIG V-222576: Omitting the Secure flag permits cookies to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling session hijacking.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Set SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always to ensure cookies are only sent over HTTPS.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A05 / CIS Level 2: A wildcard CORS policy allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests, undermining same-origin protection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with an explicit allowlist: .WithOrigins("https://trusted-domain.com"). Never combine AllowAnyOrigin() with AllowCredentials().

forbidden_patterns.reason: NIST SP 800-52 / DISA STIG V-222596: TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are deprecated and contain known cryptographic weaknesses.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Restrict to TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only: SslProtocols.Tls12 | SslProtocols.Tls13 or SecurityProtocolType.Tls12 | SecurityProtocolType.Tls13.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-38A: ECB mode is deterministic and does not provide semantic security; identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks, leaking data patterns.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with AesGcm (AES-256-GCM) for authenticated encryption, or use CipherMode.CBC with a random IV and an HMAC for integrity.

forbidden_patterns.reason: NIST SP 800-131A: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is vulnerable to padding oracle (Bleichenbacher) attacks and is deprecated for new applications.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with RSAEncryptionPadding.OaepSHA256 (or stronger) for all RSA encryption operations.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A09 / NIST AU-3: Enabling EF Core's sensitive data logging writes parameter values (including passwords and PII) to application logs, creating a credential and data exposure risk.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove or set EnableSensitiveDataLogging(false) in all non-development environments. Never enable sensitive data logging in production.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded API keys and secret keys in source code expose credentials to anyone with code access or in version-control history.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded secrets. Load from environment variables (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable) or a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).

forbidden_patterns.reason: NIST SP 800-132 / OWASP Password Storage: PBKDF2 with fewer than 600,000 iterations provides insufficient resistance against brute-force attacks. OWASP recommends at least 600,000 iterations for SHA-256.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use at least 600,000 iterations with HashAlgorithmName.SHA256 via Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(), or prefer Argon2id for new applications.
